newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-LASORDA HAS SECOND ANGIOPLASTY AND REPORTED DOING WELL.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-LASORDA HAS SECOND ANGIOPLASTY AND REPORTED DOING WELL.

text.p: Former Los Angeles Dodgers' manager Tommy Lasorda Friday night underwent his second angioplasty operation in less than four months after suffering chest pains, the team said.
Lasorda, 69, was admitted to Centinela Hospital Medical Centre, and doctors determined the clogged artery cleared in a June 26 operation had closed again.
Doctors successfully repeated the procedure, the team said. Broadcast news reports said Lasorda was in excellent condition, resting comfortably and had suffered no heart damage.
Lasorda first entered the hospital in June complaining of abdominal pains, and tests showed he had suffered a mild heart attack.
The first angioplasty -- involving the insertion of a balloon-like catheter into an artery which is then inflated to remove blockage -- was performed two days later.

Lasorda, who led the Dodgers to two World Series titles and gained a reputation as one of baseball's most colourful characters, while claiming he bled Dodger Blue, retired in July after nearly 20 years as the team's manager. He then was named a team vice president.

Lasorda spent 47 years with the Dodger organisation -- as a player, scout, coach and, beginning in 1976, as manager. He was voted National League Manager of the Year three times, in 1977, 1981 and 1988.
